## Topics {.theme-title1}

::: {.incremental}
- Data communication using visualizations and report writing using the open-source quarto publishing system.
- Introduction to version control as a tool for scientific collaboration.
- R packages to create and distribute robust data analyses.
- Introduction to capabilities in the R programming language to simulate and analyze scientific ideas before data collection.
:::


## Learning Outcomes {.theme-title1}

::: {.incremental}

- Knowledge: Students...
  - have knowledge about effective data visualization and communication
  - have knowledge about version control and collaborative scientific writing

- Skills: Students...
  - can present data analyses in multiple formats based on reproducible practices using the R programming language
  - can manage collaboration in complex scientific projects
  - can write and distribute R packages, including data packages
  - can perform basic simulations and power calculations to plan for a scientific study

- General competence: Students...
  - can communicate results from complex and data-intensive analyses in suitable output formats.


:::


## Why is this a course? {.theme-title1}

::: {.incremental}
- PhD-level work requires collaboration, sharing, showing, tracability ...
- Research is a profession ...
- Most learning happens in your day-to-day activities &rarr; improve work culture
:::

## [Good habits:]{.yellow} Are not part of your course portfolio!{.smaller .scrollable .theme-title1}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Organize projects in a consistent way <!--Karl Broman  -->
- Make projects self-contained (e.g. RStudio projects/Github)
- Create and maintain documentation, start with README
- Identify one weakness in your workflow, improve and proceed with the next <!-- Karl Broman --> 
- Share your data
- Share your code
- Name files in a consistent way <!--  --->
- Stay as true as possible to a style guide
- Be lazy! Try to minimize your code (refactor when possible)
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Refactor code <!-- https://datasemantics.co/15-habits-of-highly-effective-data-scientists/  -->
- Reanalyze data sets <!-- Andrew Gelman https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2023/10/04/you-can-learn-a-lot-from-reanalyzing-data-signing-at-the-beginning-example-but-also-many-others/ -->
- Every operation in your project should be scripted <!-- Karl Broman "everything with a script" -->
- Simulate! <!-- Statistical rethinking among others -->
- Convert scripts and repeated code into functions <!-- Broman et al -->
- Document functions as part of packages <!-- Broman et al -->
- Document data
- Use version control
- Comment your code!
- Compartmentalize analyses, small scripts, incremental steps.

:::
